title: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

relationships.phenotype: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene (182810) on chromosome 9q34.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing.
checks.explanation: Paper links heterozygous SPTAN1 nonsense mutations to dominant HMN; HMND11 is OMIM's designation.

checks.claim: The SPTAN1 gene is located on chromosome 9q34.
checks.evidence_quote: heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature, not stated in abstract but acceptable.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is a form of distal hereditary motor neuropathy. Beijer et al. (2019) described the distal hereditary motor neuropathies as a rare subgroup of inherited peripheral neuropathies, hallmarked by length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant involvement of sensory neurons. Beijer et al. (2019) reported juvenile onset in HMND11.

(2019) used next-generation sequencing in 3 unrelated families with dominant juvenile-onset hereditary motor neuropathy and found heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene, which encodes alpha-II spectrin. Penetrance of the mutations varied in 2 of the 3 families.
